title: Managed disks, ephemeral OS disks and Azure Files

videos.script: A virtual machine's disks are not inside it, and they do not all behave alike. This lesson is about which disk holds what. {{managed}} A managed disk is a resource of its own. It has a type, a size and a bill, and it lives in Azure Storage, three copies of it. You will declare two for the shop's database, attach them, and choose the host caching of each. {{types}} Then the five disk types. Three are sold in size tiers, and two let you set the size, the operations per second and the throughput apart. Whatever the disk can do, the machine has a ceiling too. You will work out which one a program actually meets. {{ephemeral}} Next, an OS disk that is not kept at all. An ephemeral OS disk lives on the host, so it is fast, and it is gone when the machine leaves. For a web server that keeps nothing, that is the right trade. {{files}} Last, a share that many machines mount at once. Azure Files speaks SMB and NFS. Nothing on the laptop emulates it, so you will read it, and compile one. By the end, you can say where each piece of the shop's data should live.
